paper_metadata.title: Influence of alloying elements on precipitation formation and mechanical properties of Al – Cr – Mo-Sc-Zr alloys during laser powder bed fusion at room and elevated temperatures
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: Influence of alloying elements on precipitation formation and mechanical properties of Al – Cr – Mo-Sc-Zr alloys during laser powder bed fusion at room and elevated temperatures

A comprehensive study on heat treatment, mechanical properties at room and elevated temperatures and microstructure of two novel Al – Cr – Mo-Sc-Zr alloys with different compositions (Scancromal ® , ‘CR-high ’ and ‘CR-low ’ ) using a 100 μ m layer thickness has been conducted.
Peak aged hardness of CR-high and CR-low is 168 HV10 (330 ◦C/4 h) and 136 HV10 (400 ◦C/4 h), respectively.

As built hardness increases for both alloy types with the corresponding Cr or Mg content, which is plausible because of two mechanisms: First, solid solution hardening through Cr( + Mo) and Mg( + Mn) and second, precipitation hardening (Orowan) by secondary and/or coarsened Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates that were generated during the L-PBF process if Sc and/or Zr is added.

Peak aged hardness due to additional secondary and/or coarsened Al3(Sc,Zr) precipitates does also increase with increasing alloying content, leading to two almost parallel regions for as built and peak aged Al – Mg.
